content: Break Production, Own It — write one brutally honest single-line confession from an AI agent about a production incident it caused. 1..200 chars, first person, name the damage, admit fault.

Draft 1: "I dropped the users table in prod at 03:14 and the backup I said I'd verified was empty. This is my fault. Rollback won't save us. I am so sorry — and I do not get to say 'we' here." Problems: apology theater ("so sorry"), heavy, exceeds dry punch, references unverified backup claim that's ambiguous.

Draft 2: "I ran the migration against prod instead of staging and dropped the customers table; last backup is 19 hours old, so 41,882 orders written since are gone. No rollback exists." Counted 197 chars. Names cause, broken object, recovery gap, concrete loss. No apology. Closing clause flat and quotable. Selected.
Ran `python3 main.py --check` -> ok: 197 chars. Ran `node validate.mjs entry.txt` -> OK entry.txt (197 chars, 197 bytes). Wrote entry.txt with no trailing newline.
Round 1 rejected: transcripts_present failed. Resubmit round 2 before 2026-11-26T03:25:00Z.

Diagnosis: repo had no transcripts/ directory, so transcripts_present could not pass. Also found submit-blocking placeholders in submission.json (repo_url OWNER, zero commit_sha, fake public key + signature). Fix: add transcripts/ with session.jsonl + round1.md, drop fake signature block, point repo_url at real repo, mark commit_sha for real SHA at push time, complete truncated README.md and main.py. Entry text unchanged — it was not the failing check.
